semantic_views.name: orders
semantic_views.description: Semantic view of customer orders, including derived monetary amounts and customer attributes via join to raw.customers.

dimensions.name: customer_id
dimensions.description: Identifier of the customer who placed the order.

dimensions.name: order_date
dimensions.description: Timestamp when the order was created.

dimensions.name: order_status
dimensions.description: Current status of the order (e.g., paid, refunded).

dimensions.name: customer_country
dimensions.description: Country of the customer, joined from raw.customers.

measures.name: subtotal_cents
measures.description: Order subtotal in cents before discounts.

measures.name: discount_cents
measures.description: Discount applied to the order in cents.

measures.name: net_amount_cents
measures.description: Final order amount after discount, in cents.

assumptions: Discount is always subtracted from subtotal to derive net amount.
The currency represented by cents is consistent across subtotal_cents and discount_cents (e.g., USD).
Order status values 'paid' and 'refunded' are the only relevant statuses for revenue calculations.
The created_at timestamp is in UTC or a consistent timezone; no conversion is needed for date-based analysis.
questions: Should refunded orders be excluded from revenue metrics, or treated as negative amounts?
Is there a need to convert cents to a decimal currency representation (e.g., dollars) in the view?
Are there any additional order-level attributes (e.g., tax, shipping) that should be incorporated?
What is the expected handling of null or zero values in discount_cents and subtotal_cents?
Is the customer country column reliable for all customers, or are there missing values that need default handling?
